1.Finding the Tangent or Cotangent of a Special Angle?

tan⁡(11π6)=

M
Tue, Mar 3rd @ 2:16 PM|Elapsed: 2:14Correct

Let's remind ourselves of the special trigonometric ratios, as given by the unit circle.

From the unit circle, we see that the angle 11π6 corresponds to the point (32,−12).

  • Since the cosine of the angle corresponds to the x-coordinate, we have cos⁡(11π6)=32.

  • Since the sine of the angle corresponds to the y-coordinate, we have sin⁡(11π6)=−12.

Therefore, using the fact that tan⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ, we have

tan⁡(11π6)=sin⁡(11π6)cos⁡(11π6)=(−12)(32)=−13.

Therefore, using the fact that csc⁡θ=1sin⁡θ, we have

csc⁡(7π4)=1sin⁡(7π4)=−22=−2.
